_comment: The 1805 campaign opening (Sept 25, 1805 anchor - the Grande Armee crossing the Rhine). Authored against the landed 1805 Loader + Constants pre-slice contract: sovereign_map europe, regions OMITTED (the validated 126-province world is injected), ordered France-first starting_wars (ONE shared coalition instance, Britain defender leader), coalition seeded via active_coalition/threat_level/coalition_count. Boot via SOVEREIGN_SCENARIO=<path to this file>. Source of truth: docs/MAP_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md SS'Researched 1805 opening draft' (design gate BLESSED July 1, 2026). Supply-cap deviations of record (July 1, 2026): Ney<->Soult provinces swapped (Rhineland stack fit), Mack 58k->52k + Charles 65k->54k (Carniola home cap; preserves Charles > Mack), Milan registry terrain corrected mountains->plains (Po plain; Massena supply). DEF-6 (Slice 8, July 2, 2026): region_overrides stamps a 12,000 Flanders garrison (the Boulogne rear depot / Channel-coast pickets) so the London<->Flanders sea link is never a free walk into France; capital garrisons are tier-differentiated by the loader (majors 25k / secondary 15k / minors 10k). DEF-5 naval follow-up (Aug 2, 2026): the registry gained the London<->Normandy sea link - the SHORT Channel crossing (111px vs Flanders's 352px) and the historic descent beach - so a British landing comes ashore on the Norman coast instead of only through the Low Countries, where the Flanders<->Orleanais edge fed straight into the French interior. Normandy carries the same 12,000 Channel-coast depot as Flanders (the DEF-6 rule: a beachhead is never a free walk-in), which matters doubly because Normandy is one march from Paris.
scenario_description: September 25, 1805. The Grande Armee wheels from the Channel to the Rhine. Britain, Austria and Russia stand in arms; Mack's Austrians have crossed the Inn into Bavaria; Kutuzov marches west. Sweden and Naples lean toward the Coalition but have not yet drawn the sword. Prussia watches, armed and neutral.
_campaign_end_comment: GE-1 The Verdict and the Fall (docs/GAME_END_SPEC.md R1/R2/R7, docs/ENDGAME_PLAN.md section 3): the block that ARMS the campaign's endings - its presence is the flag (never sandbox_mode). verdict_turn 44 = Early July 1807, the summer of Tilsit: at the end of that turn a ceremonial Verdict of History grades the reign and the campaign continues. fall_grace_turns 5 = The Empire Without Soil or Sword (at most one province, or no free corps and no affordable commission, while at war). captivity_grace_turns 10 = The Eagle in Chains (the Emperor a prisoner, counted while at war with his captor). title_turns 12 = the quiet possession after which a conquest is titled (ENDGAME_PLAN section 2.2; read by GE-3's Congress). All in-band tunable; the tutorial authors no block and never arms.
_congress_comment: GE-3 The Congress of Paris (docs/ENDGAME_PLAN.md section 2, RULED): with hold_titled provinces held by TITLE the Emperor may summon the Congress; every great power answers every turn (recognition_threshold on the at-peace formula; a court at war sues at sue_score or when its capital falls; Britain is shut out at cs_shutout_pct of the Continent's ports); it sits congress_turns turns while refusers harden refuser_weight_per_turn a turn, the coalition gate drops to congress_alarm_gate and the hold must stand (alarm below hold_alarm_ceiling); all signed, shut out or gone on the last turn = THE IMPERIAL PEACE, else it dissolves (dissolve_alarm, congress_cooldown). The sweetener buys sweetener_per_1000 a thousand gold, capped at sweetener_cap. All in-band tunable.
_economy_balance_comment: SR-5a The chest (Score Mandate Chunk 5, RULED by the user September 28, 2026 - docs/SCORE_MANDATE_PLAN.md section 2 Chunk 5, rules docs/SYSTEMS_REFERENCE.md section 76): Britain is the richest court in Europe and France pays for its war by conquest. region_overrides carries each province's income_value: every French homeland province yields three-quarters of the registry figure (3,400 -> 2,590 gold; the Emperor's 1805 treasury was in crisis until Austerlitz) and England's five industrial and commercial provinces rise (London 500, East Anglia 300, Midlands 300, Northumbria 150, Scotland 150; 1,500 -> 2,050). With the navies block (Britain trade_dominance 300 -> 450, overseas_income 500 -> 1,000) Britain nets 2,851 a turn at boot against France's 1,032 (it was 1,901 against 1,842); France's turn-1 absorption is 67%, inside the 55-70% band the EC-2 gate blessed. Scenario-scoped: the registry, the tutorial and the legacy world keep their figures.
_variance_comment: AI-0c (docs/AI_INTENT_SPEC.md 3.8.1, D7): authored variance bands. A relation entry may be a band-carrying object {value, band:[lo,hi]} - the campaign seed resolves it inside the band; the historical seed (or unset SOVEREIGN_SEED) always resolves to `value`, today's boot byte-for-byte. No band = no variance. Banded here: Prussia's disposition (the definitional 1805 contingency), the starting grudges (Austria-Prussia over Germany, Russia-Ottoman over the straits, Prussia-Hanover), the minors' lean, and the intra-coalition warmth that picks Britain's first subsidy client. starting_wars pairs are deliberately unbanded (the validator would clamp any band to below the -60 armistice-first line). threat_level_band varies the campaign's central pressure narrowly - widening it escalates.

Ney.name: Ney

ability.name: Bravest of the Brave
ability.description: Ney's aggressive leadership inspires devastating attacks

Ney.biography: VI Corps - crossed the Rhine opposite Durlach on September 26. The bravest of the brave leads infantry now; the Cavalry Reserve rides with Murat.

Davout.name: Davout

ability.name: Iron Resolve
ability.description: The iron marshal coils behind his earthworks - patient discipline becomes a hammer-blow when III Corps springs
ability.effect: Each fortified turn builds +1 resolve stack (max 3). His next attack consumes all stacks for +8% each (max +24%). Stacks survive unfortify but clear if he moves or is routed.

Davout.biography: III Corps - crossed the Rhine at Mannheim on September 26. The iron marshal, exacting and incorruptible.

Soult.name: Soult

ability.name: Drillmaster of Boulogne
ability.description: Soult drilled the camps of Boulogne to clockwork - his corps sharpens in a single day
ability.effect: Drill completes in 1 turn (not 2) and never locks him out of your orders

Soult.biography: IV Corps - marching for the Speyer crossing from its Lorraine camps, 10,000 of its best carved away to form the Emperor's Guard. A superb tactician who executes the Emperor's plan to the letter, exactly on the appointed hour.

Lannes.name: Lannes

ability.name: Roland of the Army
ability.description: Lannes marches to the sound of the guns - the second wave that (almost) always comes

Lannes.biography: V Corps - crossed at Kehl on September 25, pressing the Black Forest feint.

Murat.name: Murat

ability.name: First Horseman of Europe
ability.description: When Murat personally breaks an enemy, his cavalry turns the rout into annihilation
ability.effect: +5,000 pursuit casualties when an enemy he defeats is forced to retreat (cavalry, leading the attack)

Murat.biography: The Cavalry Reserve - screening the Black Forest feint while the army wheels north of the Danube.

Bernadotte.name: Bernadotte

ability.name: Eyes on a Crown
ability.description: Bernadotte weighs every order against his own ambitions - the I Corps does not always march
ability.effect: +10% defiance after insisted objections; -15 reinforcement arrival score (a written support order mostly cancels it)

Bernadotte.biography: I Corps at Wuerzburg, marched down from occupied Hanover - standing on allied Bavarian soil across Mack's rear.

Massena.name: Massena

ability.name: Child of Victory
ability.description: Cornered and outnumbered is where Massena fights best

Massena.biography: The Army of Italy on the Adige, facing Archduke Charles - the dear child of victory, chafing on the defensive: set to hold the second front, but itching to throw his corps across the river at the Austrians.

Napoleon.name: Napoleon

ability.name: The Presence
ability.description: His presence on the field was worth forty thousand men - Wellington
ability.effect: Every French corps fighting in the Emperor's province gains +10% attack and defense. Enemy commanders will not attack his army at odds they would accept against any marshal.

Napoleon.biography: Emperor of the French, on the Rhine with the Guard - 10,000 men carved from Soult's own IV Corps, and Soult's corps is drawn up beside them. He left Paris on the 24th of September and the army is across the river; Mack sits at Ulm one march east. The Grande Armee is his instrument; the Empire is his estate; the marshals shine only in his light - or out of it.

Deroy.name: Deroy
Deroy.biography: The Bavarian field army - two divisions under Deroy and Wrede, withdrawn to Wuerzburg rather than submit to Austria, now under French operational direction.

Mack.name: Mack
Mack.biography: The Army of Germany, camped around Ulm on invaded Bavarian soil - quartermaster's plans and paper certainties, deep in hostile country.

ArchdukeCharles.name: ArchdukeCharles

ability.name: Habsburg Resolve
ability.description: Archduke Charles steadies the line with calm under fire

ArchdukeCharles.biography: Austria's main army behind the Adige - the Habsburgs' best soldier, husbanding his strength for the Italian front.

ArchdukeJohn.name: ArchdukeJohn
ArchdukeJohn.biography: The Army of Tyrol at Innsbruck, hinging the German and Italian theaters.

Kutuzov.name: Kutuzov

ability.name: The Old Fox
ability.description: Kutuzov's fighting retreat is his art - chasing him is a half-harvest trap
ability.effect: Pursuit casualties against him halved; retreat-path attrition halved

Kutuzov.biography: The Army of Podolia marching west to join Austria - the one-eyed old fox, weeks away still.

Buxhowden.name: Buxhowden
Buxhowden.biography: The Army of Volhynia, the second echelon - weeks behind Kutuzov on its namesake ground.

Moore.name: Moore

ability.name: Shorncliffe System
ability.description: Moore's recruits arrive drilled - Britain rebuilds quality, not just numbers
ability.effect: Troops he recruits arrive at morale 60 (green conscripts arrive at 40)

Moore.biography: Major-General Sir John Moore, home command at Shorncliffe - trainer of the finest light infantry in Europe.

Brunswick.name: Brunswick
Brunswick.biography: The Duke of Brunswick, Prussia's senior field marshal - the army in home cantonments, armed and neutral.

Hohenlohe.name: Hohenlohe
Hohenlohe.biography: Prince Hohenlohe's corps in Silesia, watching the Russian marches on the tense northern flank.

Armfelt.name: Armfelt
Armfelt.biography: Gustav Mauritz Armfelt, commander of Sweden's Pomeranian expedition - the king's sword, not yet drawn.

Damas.name: Damas
Damas.biography: Roger de Damas, reorganizer of the Bourbon army - Naples plays its double game, a neutrality treaty in one hand and the Coalition's promises in the other.

Frederick.name: Frederick
Frederick.biography: Crown Prince Frederick, regent of Denmark - the army concentrated in Holstein, guarding an armed neutrality.

Castanos.name: Castanos
Castanos.biography: Castanos, Commandant-General of the Campo de Gibraltar - Spain's war with Britain is fought at sea; Trafalgar is four weeks out.

Abdurrahman.name: Abdurrahman
Abdurrahman.biography: Kadi Abdurrahman Pasha, governor of Karaman, with the Nizam-i Cedid new-model troops - the Porte's reformed army, far from Europe's quarrel.

Zezschwitz.name: Zezschwitz
Zezschwitz.biography: Hans Gottlob von Zezschwitz - the old general of the Elector's troops, mobilised as an observation corps of 15,000 in the autumn of 1805; at Jena he held the Saxon line under Hohenlohe until hope was gone.

BernardimFreire.name: BernardimFreire
BernardimFreire.biography: Bernardim Freire de Andrade - a careful, prickly general of a neutral court's unmobilised army; in 1808 he led Portugal's northern army beside Wellesley, who found him hard to work with.

_marshal_pool_comment: Marshal Recruitment (docs/MARSHAL_RECRUITMENT_SPEC.md): commissionable candidates per nation, authored quality order (the AI takes the first affordable). No location/strength - the corps is raised at commission (5,000 infantry from the pool). cost = gold. Relationship seeds apply symmetrically to marshals in service. The secondaries' benches (EG-D3, ruled October 13, 2026; built in SF-RR4): Spain's La Romana, Blake and Cuesta, Sweden's Toll and Adlercreutz, Bavaria's Wrede - each court at war commissions from its own, as the great powers do. S14k (ruled October 28, 2026 - the user: 'they should get armies or the ability to make them'): the courts that had none - Portugal's Silveira, Saxony's Le Coq, Hesse's Emil, Hanover's Wallmoden and Alten, Holland's Janssens, the Kingdom of Italy's Fontanelli, Switzerland's Wattenwyl and Bachmann - and the one-general courts' second men, Denmark's Christian August, Naples' Philippsthal, the Ottomans' Alemdar and Yusuf Ziya. A court commissions at war, preparing a design, or called to arms by a design priced against it; a satellite serving its lord's war fights by its contingent, and its bench is for a war of its own. Sardinia and the Papal States keep their garrisons only: neither fielded an army in the period.

France.name: Mortier
France.biography: Edouard Mortier - steady, imperturbable, and universally liked - one of the few marshals who has made no enemies in the army.

France.name: Grouchy
France.biography: Emmanuel de Grouchy - precise, methodical, France's finest cavalry tactician after Murat. Executes his orders to the letter; expect nothing beyond them.

France.name: Suchet
France.biography: Louis-Gabriel Suchet - the best administrator in the army. Provinces prosper under his hand; his troops are always paid, always fed.

France.name: Oudinot
France.biography: Nicolas Oudinot - the grenadier's grenadier, collector of thirty-four wounds. Leads from the front because he knows no other place.

France.name: Augereau
France.biography: Pierre Augereau - the brawler of Castiglione, a duelist risen from the gutters of Paris. Past his best years, still dangerous in a fight.

France.name: Marmont
France.biography: Auguste Marmont - artillery savant, companion of the Emperor's youth, and the most nakedly ambitious officer in France.

France.name: Senarmont
France.biography: Alexandre de Senarmont - master of the massed battery, who rolls the guns forward to shatter a line at the decisive hour. France's artillery is the finest in Europe, and her gunners the cheapest to raise.

Austria.name: Schwarzenberg
Austria.biography: Karl Philipp zu Schwarzenberg - the diplomat-soldier. Careful, patient, and impossible to provoke into a battle he has not already won.

Austria.name: Hiller
Austria.biography: Johann von Hiller - methodical, quarrelsome, and exact. Holds whatever he is told to hold, and files a protest afterward.

Austria.name: Liechtenstein
Austria.biography: Johann von Liechtenstein - the cavalry prince. Charges first, negotiates after.

Austria.name: Smola
Austria.biography: Josef Smola - Austria's foremost gunner, a lifelong artillerist who lays a massed battery with a duelist's eye.

Russia.name: Bagration
Russia.biography: Pyotr Bagration - the fiery Georgian, Suvorov's favorite pupil. Give him the rearguard and he becomes a wall; give him the vanguard and he becomes a spear.

Russia.name: Bennigsen
Russia.biography: Levin von Bennigsen - the stubborn Hanoverian in Russian service. Unlovable, unbreakable, and unforgiving of rivals.

Russia.name: Dokhturov
Russia.biography: Dmitry Dokhturov - the unshakeable. Small, ill, half-deaf, and utterly immovable from any post entrusted to him.

Russia.name: Kutaisov
Russia.biography: Alexander Kutaisov - the young prodigy of the Russian guns, brilliant, beloved, and brave to a fault.

Prussia.name: Blucher
Prussia.biography: Gebhard von Blucher - Marshal Forwards. Seventy years of fury on horseback; the only general in Europe who attacks as instinctively as Ney.

Prussia.name: Scharnhorst
Prussia.biography: Gerhard von Scharnhorst - the quiet Hanoverian professor who intends to rebuild the Prussian army from its foundations.

Prussia.name: Yorck
Prussia.biography: Ludwig Yorck - dour, exact, and stiff-necked. Obeys the letter of every order and trusts no one, least of all his superiors.

Prussia.name: Holtzendorff
Prussia.biography: Karl von Holtzendorff - keeper of the King's artillery reserve, methodical and precise where the Prussian line is not.

Britain.name: Wellesley
Britain.biography: Arthur Wellesley - the Sepoy General, home from India with a reputation and a plan. Picks his ground, holds it, and never fights the battle his enemy wants.

Britain.name: Paget
Britain.biography: Henry Paget - the finest cavalry officer Britain owns, and the boldest. His charges end in glory or in Spain.

Britain.name: Shrapnel
Britain.biography: Henry Shrapnel - Royal Artillery officer whose spherical case-shot bursts above a line and scythes it down; Britain's guns are few but deadly.

Spain.name: LaRomana
Spain.biography: Pedro Caro, Marquis of La Romana - he spirited the Spanish division Napoleon had borrowed home from Denmark aboard British ships in 1808, and kept the Army of the Left alive in the Galician hills.

Spain.name: Blake
Spain.biography: Joaquin Blake - born in Malaga to an Irish family, the founder of Spain's general staff: brave, methodical, and beaten at Medina de Rioseco, Espinosa and Sagunto.

Spain.name: Cuesta
Spain.biography: Gregorio Garcia de la Cuesta - the old captain-general of Castile, near seventy; he never refused a battle, quarrelled with Blake at Medina de Rioseco, and was ridden down at Medellin.

Sweden.name: Toll
Sweden.biography: Johan Christopher Toll - Gustav III's soldier-administrator and the governor of Swedish Pomerania, who brought the army off Rugen by treaty when Stralsund fell in 1807.

Sweden.name: Adlercreutz
Sweden.biography: Carl Johan Adlercreutz - the victor of Siikajoki and Revolax in the Finnish War, and in 1809 the officer who arrested his own king.

Bavaria.name: Wrede
Bavaria.biography: Carl Philipp von Wrede - the Bavarian army's field commander from Ulm to Wagram, Deroy's rival for the King's favour; he led the Bavarians into Russia in 1812 and against Napoleon at Hanau in 1813.

Portugal.name: Silveira
Portugal.biography: Francisco da Silveira - bold to the edge of rashness; he retook Chaves in 1809 and held the bridge at Amarante against Soult for a fortnight.

Saxony.name: LeCoq
Saxony.biography: Karl Christian Erdmann von Le Coq - a prudent Saxon general who led his division at Grossbeeren and Dennewitz in 1813 and the Saxon corps in the Netherlands in 1814.

Hesse.name: Emil
Hesse.biography: Prince Emil of Hesse - an energetic young prince who led the Hessian troops from 1809, into Russia in 1812 and on to Leipzig in 1813.

Hanover.name: Wallmoden
Hanover.biography: Ludwig von Wallmoden-Gimborn - calm and methodical; he commanded the allied corps on the Lower Elbe in 1813 and beat Pecheux at the Gohrde.

Hanover.name: Alten
Hanover.biography: Charles Alten - a Hanoverian of the King's German Legion who led the Light Division in Spain and the 3rd Division at Waterloo; steady under orders, never one to improvise.

Holland.name: Janssens
Holland.biography: Jan Willem Janssens - a dutiful Dutch general who fought for the Cape in 1806 and for Java in 1811, each time against the odds.

KingdomOfItaly.name: Fontanelli
KingdomOfItaly.biography: Achille Fontanelli - the Kingdom of Italy's prudent minister of war; he fought at Raab in 1809 and held the rearguard at Hanau in 1813.

Switzerland.name: Wattenwyl
Switzerland.biography: Niklaus Rudolf von Wattenwyl - General of the Confederation in 1805, 1809 and 1813; he guarded Swiss neutrality and shunned a fight he could not win.

Switzerland.name: Bachmann
Switzerland.biography: Niklaus Franz von Bachmann - the old professional who led the Swiss army into Franche-Comte in 1815.

Denmark.name: ChristianAugust
Denmark.biography: Prince Christian August of Augustenborg - commander in Norway, who turned back the Swedish invasion of 1808 at Prestebakke and Toverud.

Naples.name: Philippsthal
Naples.biography: Prince Louis of Hesse-Philippsthal - the defiant governor of Gaeta, who held the fortress against Massena for five months in 1806: 'Gaeta is not Ulm'.

Ottoman.name: Alemdar
Ottoman.biography: Alemdar Mustafa Pasha - the ayan of Ruse, who raised the Danube's defence against Russia in 1806-07 and marched on Constantinople in 1808 to restore the New Order.

Ottoman.name: YusufZiya
Ottoman.biography: Yusuf Ziya Pasha - twice Grand Vizier; he led the army that retook Egypt beside the British in 1801 and commanded against Russia from 1809.

_contingents_comment: VD-C 'The Contingent' (docs/VASSAL_DEEPENING_SPEC.md section 9.1): the commanders a satellite sends at the head of its contingent when it shares its lord's war - the first who is not serving, not fallen and not on any bench; past the list, '<Adjective> Contingent'. The bench's candidate shape, never commissioned (no cost). Authored for the boot satellites and the courts most likely to become one, each a general who led his court's contingent beside the French: Dumonceau's Batavian division with Marmont in 1805, Teulie's Italians the same year, Amey's Swiss at the Berezina, Raglovich's Bavarians in Saxony in 1813, Thielmann's Saxons, Poniatowski's Poles, Kindelan's Spaniards in Denmark (who stayed when La Romana walked out in 1808), Grawert's Prussian auxiliary corps of 1812. Wrede and La Romana sit their own courts' benches (EG-D3), so a court's commission and its contingent never share a man.

Holland.name: Dumonceau
Holland.biography: Jean-Baptiste Dumonceau - a Brussels-born general of the Batavian army; his Dutch division marched with Marmont's corps to the Danube in 1805.

Holland.name: Daendels
Holland.biography: Herman Willem Daendels - patriot of 1795 and the Batavian army's restless organiser; he led the Dutch into Germany in 1806.

Holland.name: Chasse
Holland.biography: David Hendrik Chasse - 'General Bayonet' to the French for his charges in Spain; a Dutch brigadier who never waited to be ordered forward.

KingdomOfItaly.name: Teulie
KingdomOfItaly.biography: Pietro Teulie - Milanese patriot and minister of war; he led the Italian division north with the Grande Armee in 1805 and fell before Kolberg in 1807.

KingdomOfItaly.name: Pino
KingdomOfItaly.biography: Domenico Pino - the Italian army's fighting general; his division stormed in Spain and held at Maloyaroslavets in 1812.

KingdomOfItaly.name: Lechi
KingdomOfItaly.biography: Giuseppe Lechi - a Brescian cavalryman who commanded the Italian division that held Barcelona in 1808.

Switzerland.name: Amey
Switzerland.biography: Francois Pierre Amey - a Swiss officer in French service; he brought the Swiss regiments across the Berezina in 1812.

Bavaria.name: Raglovich
Bavaria.biography: Clemens von Raglovich - he kept the Bavarian division under the eagles through the Saxon campaign of 1813, until his King changed sides at Ried.

Saxony.name: Thielmann
Saxony.biography: Johann von Thielmann - a Saxon cavalry general; his cuirassiers charged the Great Redoubt at Borodino, and he went over to the allies in 1813.

DuchyOfWarsaw.name: Poniatowski
DuchyOfWarsaw.biography: Jozef Poniatowski - nephew of the last king of Poland and the Duchy's minister of war; he led the Polish corps to Moscow and died at Leipzig a Marshal of France.

DuchyOfWarsaw.name: Dabrowski
DuchyOfWarsaw.biography: Jan Henryk Dabrowski - founder of the Polish Legions in Italy; he raised the Poles of Posen in 1806.

Spain.name: Kindelan
Spain.biography: Juan Kindelan - La Romana's second in Denmark in 1808, who stayed with the French when the division sailed home.

Denmark.name: Ewald
Denmark.biography: Johann von Ewald - a Danish general of light troops who hunted Schill's raiders to Stralsund in 1809.

Portugal.name: Gomes Freire
Portugal.biography: Gomes Freire de Andrade - commander of the Portuguese Legion in French service, which marched to Russia in 1812.

Prussia.name: Grawert
Prussia.biography: Julius von Grawert - first commander of the Prussian auxiliary corps that marched with the Grande Armee in 1812.

_statecraft_comment: AI-3r section 2.6 (docs/AI_WAR_DECISION_SPEC.md, gate ruling R1): authored rear-security posture. wary_of multiplies the neighbour's menace in the war council's reserve calculus - a fear the relations number alone would understate. v1 authors wary_of ONLY (profile keys stay in nation_config). Values clamp-validated to [0.5, 2.0]; absent pair = 1.0. Authored 1805 fears: the German dualism both ways (Silesia taken 1742 - Berlin and Vienna each garrison against the other), Prussia's dread of the Russian colossus marching through Poland, the standing Russo-Turkish menace on the straits (the 1806 war), and Sweden's fear for Finland (lost 1809).
_agendas_comment: Nation Agendas NA-0 (docs/NATION_AGENDAS_SPEC.md section 4): authored historical decks. Deck order = priority - the first agenda whose predicate holds is ACTIVE. Vassals never activate agendas while vassalized (the KingdomOfItaly and Holland decks lie DORMANT at boot and wake on independence). Nations without decks get the survival override only. AI-0c deck-order band: entries sharing an `order_group` value (contiguous run) are equally-live designs the campaign seed may reorder; the historical seed keeps authored order. Austria's pair carries the phase's one order band - the Vienna war council's real debate, Italy-first (Charles) vs Germany-first (Mack). Russia's deck is deliberately unbanded (pin 22): arbiter_of_europe leads on every seed and gulf_and_straits stays behind it at boot. S14k (ruled October 28, 2026 - the user: 'it should be possible for underdog stories ... generally the same but some runs are surprising'): the courts that had no deck have goals - Saxony's Wettin Crown and Hesse's Westphalian Duchy (acquiring, their courts sleepier than the ladder's default, so the moment wakes them), and the neutral postures of Portugal, Hanover and Switzerland; Denmark's Scania and the Porte's Black Sea Shore stand behind their neutrality and wake only in a war.

Austria.title: Redeem Italy
Austria.blurb: The priority theater of 1805 - Charles holds the main army in Italy; the losses of Campo Formio and Luneville must be undone.

Austria.title: Primacy in Germany
Austria.blurb: Mack's thrust to the Iller - Bavaria's defection to France must be punished and the German lands held for the Habsburg crown.

Austria.title: The Eastern Question
Austria.blurb: The Porte is failing, and the Habsburg frontier runs where the Turk is weakest. If Italy and Germany are closed to Vienna, the Danube and the Adriatic are not: Albania and Rumelia would make the House of Austria the master of the Balkans before St Petersburg can be.

Prussia.title: The Hanoverian Prize
Prussia.blurb: Napoleon dangles the Electorate at Schoenbrunn; Berlin covets it openly. The buy-Prussia lever.

Prussia.title: Armed Neutrality
Prussia.blurb: North Germany is Prussia's yard - a belligerent marching through it, as at Ansbach, enrages Berlin.

Britain.title: The Low Countries
Britain.blurb: The Scheldt obsession - the invasion coast may not stay in French hands. London will not rest while the bloc holds it.

Britain.title: The Paymaster of Coalitions
Britain.blurb: Pitt's gold - 1.25 million pounds per hundred thousand men, the subsidy conventions of 1805.

Russia.title: Arbiter of Europe
Russia.blurb: Alexander campaigns as the guardian of the European order - the Tsar fights the hegemon while the coalition stands.

Russia.title: The Gulf and the Straits
Russia.blurb: Petersburg is shielded on the Gulf and completed at the Straits - the Tsar's two shores. A design that waits behind the war with France, and wakes the day that war is no longer the Tsar's concern.

Sweden.title: Scourge of the Usurper
Sweden.blurb: Gustav IV's personal anti-Napoleon zeal - the King of Sweden treats the Emperor as a usurper to be unmade.

Ottoman.title: Guard the Straits
Ottoman.blurb: The Porte stays neutral; the Straits are inviolate.

Ottoman.title: The Black Sea Shore
Ottoman.blurb: The Crimea and the Yedisan, lost to Russia between 1774 and 1792 - the Porte's revanche, once it is at war.

Sardinia.title: The House of Savoy Restored
Sardinia.blurb: The court in Cagliari wants its mainland back.

Denmark.title: Neutrality of the North
Denmark.blurb: Armed neutrality - the fleet is the state.

Denmark.title: Scania
Denmark.blurb: Scania, lost to Sweden in 1658 - Copenhagen's war aim the day the North goes to war, as it did in 1808.

KingdomOfItaly.title: Risorgimento
KingdomOfItaly.blurb: The dream the vassal wakes with - a free Italian crown gathering the peninsula. Dormant while Milan answers to Paris.

forms.blurb: By the will of the nation and the fortune of arms - the KINGDOM OF ITALY is no more. ITALY stands.

KingdomOfItaly.title: Guard the Peninsula
KingdomOfItaly.blurb: A nation that has just made itself consolidates. The peninsula is gathered; now it is held - and a foreign column crossing it is an insult to a country that exists.

Holland.title: The Seventeen Provinces
Holland.blurb: A free Holland reaching for the Austrian-Netherlands inheritance. Dormant while Amsterdam answers to Paris.

forms.blurb: The inheritance of Burgundy is gathered under one crown - the UNITED NETHERLANDS is proclaimed at Amsterdam.

Holland.title: The Merchants' Peace
Holland.blurb: The counting houses want the sea lanes open and the armies elsewhere. A Netherlands at peace is a Netherlands that trades.

Holland.title: Ostfriesland
Holland.blurb: The Ems coast the Treaty of Fontainebleau gave Louis Bonaparte's kingdom in 1807 - the one province of Holland's own dream its lord can give, once the land is his. Dormant while Amsterdam answers to Paris.

Saxony.title: The Wettin Crown
Saxony.blurb: The Wettins wore Poland's crown for sixty-six years, and Dresden has not forgotten Warsaw - but Berlin is a friend until it is beaten.

Hesse.title: The Westphalian Duchy
Hesse.blurb: Darmstadt has held the Duchy of Westphalia since 1803; a Hesse grown strong would take the whole of it while its neighbour is down.

Portugal.title: The Old Alliance
Portugal.blurb: England's oldest ally keeps its ports open and its frontier shut - a neutral court that marches only when it must.

Hanover.title: The Electorate
Hanover.blurb: The King of England's German lands ask only to be left alone - and remember who did not leave them so.

Switzerland.title: The Confederation
Switzerland.blurb: Armed neutrality, the Diet's oldest policy - the cantons call up their contingents when an army nears the frontier.

_formable_nations_comment: Nation Agendas NA-6c (docs/NATION_AGENDAS_SPEC.md section 11.4): Class C carve-out templates. A conquering side may carve one of these client states out of the DEFEATED party's soil at the settlement table, via the create_client clause. NONE of these tags exist at boot - the block is a catalogue of what MAY be erected, not a roster. Any side may carve (GR5): the Duchy of Normandy is the coalition-side mirror, carved from French home soil. 'provinces' must ALL be held by the carving side and must ALL have belonged to the defeated party. 'deck' is the client's agenda deck, dormant while it remains a client (section 3.2); a deck entry carrying a 'forms' block makes the client itself formable later (the C-to-T chain). 'aggrieved' is the section 11.9 list of courts enraged by the erection itself.

DuchyOfWarsaw.blurb: Out of Prussia's Polish partition, a Polish state stands again - the DUCHY OF WARSAW is erected.

diplomat.name: Chancery of Warsaw
diplomat.biography: Speaks for a Polish state that exists at a patron's pleasure, and remembers that it did not always.

deck.title: The Commonwealth Restored
deck.blurb: A Duchy is not a kingdom. The old Commonwealth lands lie east - dormant while Warsaw answers to a foreign patron, and a red line for every court that partitioned her.

forms.blurb: The partitions are undone by the fortune of arms - the DUCHY OF WARSAW is no more. The KINGDOM OF POLAND stands.

deck.title: Guard the Vistula
deck.blurb: A country that was erased once holds what it has regathered. A foreign column on the Vistula is not a march - it is a memory.

Normandy.blurb: The old duchy is severed from the French crown - the DUCHY OF NORMANDY is erected.

diplomat.name: Chancery of Rouen
diplomat.biography: A duchy resurrected by France's enemies, and quietly aware of what that makes it.

RomanRepublic.blurb: The temporal power is ended and the tree of liberty planted on the Capitol - the ROMAN REPUBLIC is proclaimed.

diplomat.name: Chancery of the Capitol
diplomat.biography: A consul of the restored Republic, ruling from the city of the Popes and answerable to bayonets.

Ireland.blurb: The risen harp - a French bayonet holds the ring while an Irish republic is proclaimed at Dublin. Erin go bragh.

diplomat.name: Directory of United Irishmen
diplomat.biography: Wolfe Tone's heirs - a directory that owes its republic to a foreign fleet and remembers Bantry Bay, when the wind alone saved England.

deck.title: Erin Free
deck.blurb: A republic born of a naval gamble holds its two provinces against the day the Royal Navy returns. What the sea gave, the sea can take back.

_reforms_comment: SR-5r RF-0 (docs/REFORMS_SPEC.md, gate record section 0 RULED September 27, 2026; readings section 0.1 CONFIRMED). One deck per great power (R6), in the order the AI court enacts (section 7). A row is bought once (currency gold or authority, plus one admin action) and pays upkeep gold every turn as the signed Net component 'Laws'; it lapses, largest upkeep first, when the treasury cannot pay (R5), and a lapsed law may be restored within ten turns for half its price plus its arrears (R8 'The Arrears'). Nothing is in force at boot: the validator refuses enacted_turn / lapsed_turn here. effects draw from the closed set of section 4 (at most two clauses); a type not yet wired to its seam is refused ('strike, never invent'). RF-0 authors each court's Staff - the ONE actions law, the only road to a fifth action, one price for every court (section 5, Q3); the rest of the section 6 catalogue arrives with RF-2, when its effect types are wired. R6 AMENDED by S14k (October 28, 2026 - the user: 'what if ottomans reformed'): the Porte's one-row deck, the New Order (Nizam-i Cedid) - no Staff (the one-Staff rule binds the five great powers); its force_limit clause raises the Porte's force-limit floor to a great power's, and under_threat lets the AI proclaim it only at war or when a design is priced against the Porte.

France.name: The Grand Quartier Général
France.says: Berthier's headquarters grown into a true general staff: one more order carried each day.

France.name: The Train des Équipages
France.says: A military train of the state's own wagons, decreed after the Polish winter: a French army in poor or stripped country draws its full supply again - while the Grand Quartier Général stands to run it.

France.name: The Artillery Reserve
France.says: The Guard's reserve batteries and a standard gun park: artillery levies cost 15% less.

France.name: The Anticipated Class
France.date: the senatus-consultes calling the class early, 1806–07
France.says: The Senate calls each year's conscripts before their time: infantry manpower returns 25% faster.

France.name: The Berlin Decree
France.says: Every client of the Empire shuts its ports to British goods, whatever its autonomy.

France.name: The Code Abroad
France.date: the Civil Code imposed in Italy (1806), Westphalia (1807) and Warsaw (1808)
France.says: The Civil Code carried into the client states binds them to the Empire: +1 loyalty a turn in every one.

Austria.name: The Corps d'Armée
Austria.says: The Archduke's corps d'armée, the system France has used since 1800, copied at last: one more order carried each day, and the Hofkriegsrat's delays are over - the corps gather as France's do.

Austria.name: The Landwehr
Austria.says: A militia of every able man, raised by imperial patent: infantry manpower returns 25% faster.

Austria.name: The Jäger Battalions
Austria.says: Light infantry raised and trained on the French model: infantry recruits muster 10 morale higher.

Austria.name: The New Infantry Regulations
Austria.says: The Archduke's new drill book: a corps that drills recovers 5 more morale.

Austria.name: The Generalissimus
Austria.says: The Archduke placed over the Aulic Council: every levy costs 10% less.

Prussia.name: The General Staff
Prussia.says: Scharnhorst's General Staff, built on the French headquarters that beat Prussia: one more order carried each day.

Prussia.name: The Krümper System
Prussia.says: Men trained in rotation and sent home, a reserve beyond the treaty's limit: infantry manpower returns 25% faster.

Prussia.name: The Articles of War
Prussia.says: Flogging abolished and promotion opened to merit: infantry recruits muster 10 morale higher, and - once the General Staff stands - the army is no longer brittle: a lopsided defeat costs what it costs France.

Prussia.name: The Military Reorganisation Commission
Prussia.says: Scharnhorst's commission remakes the army on the French pattern: a corps that drills recovers 5 more morale.

Prussia.name: The Emancipation Edict
Prussia.says: Serfdom ended by edict, and free men answer the levy: infantry recruits cost 10% less.

Russia.name: The Divisional System
Russia.says: Permanent divisions on the French pattern: one more order carried each day, and the columns gather as France's do - the army is no longer slow to concentrate.

Russia.name: Arakcheev's Artillery
Russia.says: Arakcheev's standard guns and parks: artillery levies cost 15% less.

Russia.name: The Opolchenie
Russia.says: The Tsar's militia called up by manifesto: infantry manpower returns 25% faster.

Russia.name: The Extraordinary Levy
Russia.says: Serfs taken from the estates by extraordinary levy: infantry recruits cost 20% less and muster 10 morale lower.

Russia.name: The War Ministry under Arakcheev
Russia.says: Arakcheev's ministry drills the army to the letter: a corps that drills recovers 5 more morale.

Britain.name: The Horse Guards Reforms
Britain.says: The Duke of York's reforms at the Horse Guards, a staff to match the French one: one more order carried each day.

Britain.name: The Orders in Council
Britain.says: Neutral trade with the blockaded ports forbidden by Order in Council: a court Britain blockades loses a quarter more of its trade.

Britain.name: The Militia Transfer
Britain.says: Castlereagh draws volunteers from the militia into the line: infantry manpower returns 25% faster, and - once the Horse Guards Reforms stand - the draft is no longer irreplaceable: recruits cost what France's do.

Britain.name: The Commissariat
Britain.says: A Commissariat able to feed an army in the field: fed supply capacity a quarter larger.

Britain.name: Congreve's Rockets
Britain.says: Congreve's rockets beside the guns: artillery levies cost 15% less.

Ottoman.name: The New Order
Ottoman.date: the Nizam-i Cedid of Selim III, 1793, to the Janissaries' revolt of 1807
Ottoman.says: Selim's drilled regiments on the European pattern: the Porte may field an army as a great power does, and its infantry drafts muster steadier - while the treasury pays the New Order its wages. The Porte proclaims it only at war, or when a design is priced against it.

_doctrines_comment: SR-7d 'The Doctrines' (docs/DOCTRINES_SPEC.md, gate record section 0 RULED September 27, 2026; readings 0.1 and the seven RV amendments CONFIRMED; built October 3, 2026). One doctrine per great power: a strength and a flaw, each a clause from the closed set (arrival_bar / attack / defense / recruit_price / defeat_morale / supply) with its number inside the validator's clamp band. In force from turn 1, never bought, never lost; only the flaw is removed - by cured_by, a law in the court's own reforms deck whose 'cures' clause names the flaw, and only while the court's Staff is in force (RV-15). Whether a flaw is cured is DERIVED from the laws at every read, never stored. A doctrine is the army's, never the man's (RV-2): no clause overrides a marshal's own character. The court's flaw never costs the man trust (RV-16). The recruit clauses price the draft, never the substitute market (RV-17). France's supply clause reads against the 1805 homeland, not the flag (RV-5): outside it, in the listed poor_country or in stripped country (war damage at or above stripped_at), a French army draws the clause's share; never on an ally's or vassal's soil. Numbers are DRAFT (in-band tunable, section 2); who a doctrine applies to and what a clause does are structural.

France.name: The Corps System
France.says: The corps march apart and fight together - and eat what the country gives them.

Britain.name: The Line Holds
Britain.says: A small army that cannot be replaced, and a line that does not give way.

Russia.name: Stubborn
Russia.says: Easier to kill than to beat - and slow to gather from the ends of an empire.
Russia.shared_on_purpose: RV-9: Russia and Austria share the flaw France's strength answers - the absence of the corps system - and both cure it by copying it (Russia's divisions, 1806; Austria's corps, 1809).

Austria.name: The Hereditary Lands
Austria.says: Beaten, and back with another army - once Vienna has written the orders.
Austria.shared_on_purpose: RV-9: the one shared clause - see Russia.

Prussia.name: Frederick's Drill
Prussia.says: Frederick's army still attacks as it did at Leuthen, and it breaks all at once.

_poor_country_comment: D-R1 (DOCTRINES_SPEC.md, CONFIRMED September 27, 2026): poor country is AUTHORED, not derived - the map marks nothing poor where history does. Where the 1807 and 1812 campaigns starved (East Prussia, Posen, Samogitia, Lithuania, White Russia, Volhynia); the Spanish war (Leon, Aragon, Galicia - the Spanish Galicia); Massena's 1810 invasion of Portugal (Alentejo, Beira); the Balkans (Rumelia, Epirus, Albania). Geography, not France's: any court whose doctrine carries a supply clause reads it. Stripped country (RV-5) is read from war damage, never authored.
_navies_comment: The Wooden Wall (docs/NAVAL_SPEC.md section 3.2): the authored 1805 navies. ONE record per nation - ships/readiness become the live fleet; ports weight the Continental System closure denominator (island rows excluded); dockyards are the build SITES (conquest grants the yard, never ships); island marks the blockade war-weariness clause + the RN blockade doctrine; trade_dominance absorbs the old Britain naval_income literal; camp_provinces are the Descent staging shores (section 5.3). Ships-0 rows are ports-only (closure denominator authored, no fleet record). Corrections vs the spec table recorded in the NV-0 landing record: Britain's third yard is East Anglia (the Nore/Medway) - the map's Wessex is drawn inland. NUI-2 (Sept 24, 2026; tools/gen_port_anchors.py): a dockyard must reach open water in the art, so three yards moved - Holland's Amsterdam -> Friesland (the Frisian coast and the Texel roadstead; the art draws Amsterdam inland), France's Channel yard Flanders -> Normandy (Le Havre and Cherbourg; the art draws Flanders inland, and it stays a camp province - Davout's camp at Bruges), Russia's Estonia -> Livonia (Riga; the art gives the province named Estonia a lake pocket, not a shore). The map draws each fleet on the water off its senior yard (the registry's port_anchor). DEF-14 (Sept 24, 2026; tools/audit_province_names.py): two yards' provinces were renamed to where the art paints them - Sweden's Scania is Stralsund (Swedish Pomerania's port, where Armfelt's army stood in 1805) and Spain's Toledo is Cartagena (the south-east coast; Spain's Mediterranean arsenal in 1805); the yards did not move. EB-2 (Econ Balance gate Aug 7 2026, ECON_BALANCE_GATE_2026_08_07.md section 3): overseas_income = the authored colonial/overseas pool, colonies as a MODIFIER never map objects - the dominance holder scales it by (1 - CS closure) like trade_dominance; a non-holder colonial power loses it under blockade and keeps a quarter while at war with the dominance holder (the RN on the sea lanes: the 1804 silver seizure). France deliberately authors NONE - its overseas arm is continental extraction (Requisitions). Britain 1,000 (SR-5a, September 28 2026, was 500) = the India/sugar trade + the fiscal machine; trade_dominance 450 (SR-5a, was 300) = the City's carrying trade; Spain 250 = American silver; Holland 150 = the East Indies; Portugal 150 = Brazil.
_imperial_designs_comment: VP-1 'The Emperor's Designs' (docs/VP1_DESIGNS_SPEC.md §2, §3, §8): France's three roads — a construction, then a seal — chosen by one irreversible proclamation on the Cabinet's road page (F1 → The Emperor's Designs). tests/fixtures/vp1_imperial_designs_block.json is pinned equal to this block.

designs.title: The Confederation of the Rhine
designs.hint: Three of Bavaria, Hesse, Saxony and Hanover under the Emperor's protection — each France's satellite at loyalty 40 or more, held four end turns.
designs.control: F1 → the court → Propose Vassal (at peace) or Subjugate (at war); Invest in Vassal keeps a member's loyalty

designs.title: A German Crown Brought to Terms
designs.hint: Austria or Prussia brought to terms: two of her own provinces or her capital ceded to the Empire (a partition), her vassalage (subjugation), or a compensated peace and her alliance within twenty turns (the moderate peace).
designs.control: F1 → Austria or Prussia → Open Settlement (the war's terms), or Propose Peace

gate.reason: the Kingdom of Italy must be France's

designs.title: The Throne of Naples
designs.hint: Naples titled to the Empire — her court France's satellite at loyalty 40 or more, or Naples held twelve quiet turns.
designs.control: F1 → Naples → Send Ultimatum (a casus belli at half the price), then Propose Vassal

designs.title: The Iron Crown
designs.hint: Milan, Piedmont and Carniola titled to the Empire, and Austria brought to terms.
designs.control: F1 → Austria → Open Settlement — Carniola ceded to the Kingdom of Italy

roads.title: The Continental System
roads.proclamation: The Blockade of the British Isles

gate.reason: France must be at war with the mistress of the seas

designs.title: The Blockade of the British Isles
designs.hint: 13 of the Continent's 26 ports shut to Britain, held six end turns — a court at war with her, in the System by a peace's clause, France's satellite, or with her capital held by a power at war with her.
designs.control: F1 → the court → a peace's Joins the Continental System clause; the Strategic Ledger's Admiralty counts the ports

designs.title: The Peace of the Continent
designs.hint: After the Blockade, Britain signs a war-ending peace with France — a great power in the System by France's clause, no lifting clause, France's own provinces whole.
designs.control: F1 → Britain → Propose Peace (no lifting clause)

acts.title: The Temple of Glory
acts.says: The Madeleine rebuilt as a temple to the Grand Army — the names of the fallen on its walls, the Empire's glory made stone.

acts.title: The Princes' Dotations
acts.says: Domains and pensions for the German princes who sit in the Confederation — their crowns guaranteed, their loyalty bought.

acts.title: The Abolition of Feudalism
acts.says: The baronies of the Kingdom of Naples abolished by decree — the Code in the south, the barons' courts closed.

acts.title: The Raft on the Niemen
acts.says: Two emperors on a raft midstream — the beaten court courted, not crushed, and asked to shut its ports against Britain.

_moments_comment: S14c 'Events and Historical Moments' (docs/EVENTS_SPEC.md §2-§5; armed by part 2's second landing): the authored letters of the record — the Bavarian Match (T8), the Throne of Holland (T18, when Holland slips), the Decree of Berlin (T29, only where it would shut a port). Each window's turn varies per campaign seed inside its band (historical = value); the Crown of the Reich (Road I, causal — a turn after the Confederation is told) armed by part 3. The staged deck tests/fixtures/moments_block.json holds the four, pinned equal.

deck.title: The Bavarian Match
deck.record: Eugène, adopted by Napoleon, wed Augusta of Bavaria at Munich (historically 14 January 1806); she had been promised to Baden's heir, and Munich yielded to the Emperor's pressing.
deck.counsel: Talleyrand — A match binds Munich to the family, Sire; Baden will remember who was passed over.

deck.title: The Throne of Holland

voice.speaker: named
voice.name: Admiral Ver Huell, for the deputation of the States General

deck.record: Historically the Dutch deputation under Admiral Ver Huell asked Napoleon for a king and was given his brother Louis (5 June 1806); Grand Pensionary Schimmelpenninck resigned rather than sign. The alternative was annexation, 1810.
deck.counsel: Talleyrand — A king of your blood in Amsterdam is a king with his own treasury, Sire.

deck.title: The Crown of the Reich
deck.record: With the Confederation signed, Napoleon told Francis II to lay down the crown of the Holy Roman Empire (historically 22 July 1806); Francis did so on 6 August, and the Reich of a thousand years ended.
deck.counsel: Talleyrand — The crown is a word, Sire; but the princes read words.

deck.title: The Decree of Berlin
deck.record: Historically, from Berlin after Jena (21 November 1806), Napoleon declared the British Isles in a state of blockade and shut every port of his allies to British goods.
deck.counsel: Decrès — The Decree shuts their ports, Sire. It does not open ours.

deck.title: The Arch-Chancellor's Letters
deck.source: research #15 — Fondation Napoléon, "Walcheren et l'affaire Fouché": the Emperor's rebuke to Cambacérès for making so little use of his powers, August 1809; Malet's forged dispatch took Paris for a morning, 23 October 1812
deck.record: Historically the Emperor governed from his camp, and in August 1809 he rebuked Cambacérès for making so little use of the powers he had left him.
deck.line: Sire, the Council sits with your orders a week on the road; the clerks ask whose hand may sign what cannot wait.
deck.watch: The Emperor afield: {n} of 6 mornings — Cambacérès may write.
deck.counsel: Berthier — Every hour you give the Council, Sire, is an hour the army waits for its orders.

accept.caption: Dictate from the field
accept.echo: Cambacérès: the Council has registered the decrees Your Majesty dictated from the field.
accept.situation: The estafette carried the Emperor's dictation to Paris; the Council sits on his orders.
accept.press: PARIS — The Council of State registers the decrees His Majesty sends from headquarters.
accept.remember: In {month} you dictated from the field; Cambacérès writes again.

decline.caption: Let the Council act
decline.echo: Cambacérès: the Council has acted in Your Majesty's name; Paris will mark whose hand signed.
decline.situation: The Council of State sat under the Arch-Chancellor; Paris remarked the Emperor's absence.
decline.press: PARIS — The Arch-Chancellor presides at the Council in His Majesty's absence.
decline.remember: In {month} you let the Council act; Cambacérès writes again.

deck.title: The Host's Claims
deck.source: research #6 — Napoleon to Berthier, 14 July 1810 (Fondation Napoléon; Branda, Le prix de la gloire): war must feed war; a corps lived on the country it stood in

voice.speaker: host
voice._tenure_comment: RE-3 (RECURRING_EVENTS_SPEC.md §12c, P6): the host's minister from the cast, unless the cast's name is out of office on the issued turn — then the chancery writes. Each gap's dates are checked against its turns by the validator alone (HC-0); the engine reads turns. Hardenberg dismissed after Schönbrunn (January 1806) and recalled April 1807; Schimmelpenninck resigned when Louis was crowned (June 1806); Cevallos lost at Bayonne (May 1808).

deck.record: Historically the Emperor's rule was that war must feed war (to Berthier, 14 July 1810): a corps lived on the country it stood in.
deck.line: Sire, {seat} has quartered and fed your corps this season; the court of {host} lays its account before you.
deck.watch: {n} corps on {host}'s soil: {m} of 3 mornings — its court may present its claims.
deck.counsel: Talleyrand — An ally presents his bill once as an account, Sire. The second time, he presents it as a grievance.

accept.caption: Pay the host's claims
accept.echo: {Minister}: the account between {host} and Paris is square for the season.
accept.situation: {seat} acknowledges the payment for the army's quarters.
accept.press: {SEAT} — The court of {host} acknowledges the scrupulous payment of the army's quarters.
accept.remember: In {month} {seat} presented its account; the court of {host} writes again.

decline.caption: Live off the land
decline.situation: The army lives on the country of {host}; {seat} keeps the account.
decline.press: {SEAT} — The Grand Army is quartered upon the country of {host}.
decline.remember: In {month} the army lived on the country of {host}; its court writes again.

deck.title: Berthier's Memorial
deck.source: REFORMS_SPEC.md §6 — the law's own record, Berthier's Imperial Headquarters, expanded 1805–07; Berthier Major-General of the Grande Armée from 1805

voice.speaker: named
voice.name: Berthier, Major-General of the Grande Armée

deck.record: Historically Berthier's Imperial Headquarters grew with every campaign from 1805 into the staff that carried the Emperor's orders.
deck.line: Sire, the orders of the day leave my tent by courier; a headquarters of the Empire would carry them under its own seal.
deck.watch: At war {n} of 4 turns, and the chest could found the headquarters — Berthier may write.
deck.counsel: Daru — The Intendance can pay for clerks, Sire. It cannot pay for an order that reaches a corps a day late.

accept.caption: Found the headquarters
accept.echo: Berthier: the Imperial Headquarters is founded; the orders of the day go out under his seal.
accept.press: HEADQUARTERS — Marshal Berthier's staff becomes the Imperial Headquarters of the Grand Army.

decline.caption: Not now
decline.remember: In {month} Berthier's memorial waited; he writes again.

deck.title: The Relief of Santo Domingo
deck.source: R1 rows 1, 2, 7 (docs/audits/AFFAIRS_DESIGN_PASS_2026_10_30.md §E.1) — S1 Reyes Sánchez 2022 (Ferrand's decree of 16 Nivôse XIII); S2 the Correspondance, 29 September 1804, 5 August 1805, 26 September 1809; S4 Leissègues at San Domingo, 6 February 1806; S15 the law of 20 May 1802 and the consular acts of 16 July and 7 December 1802

voice.speaker: named
voice.name: Decrès, Minister of Marine and the Colonies

deck.record: Historically the law of 20 May 1802 kept slavery in the colonies Amiens returned, and acts of 1802 restored it in Guadeloupe and Guiana; the expedition sent to break Toussaint Louverture's rule ended in Haiti's independence, 1 January 1804.

variants.text: Historically Missiessy's squadron reached Santo Domingo on 27 March 1805 and Dessalines raised his siege the next day; it came home whole, and the Emperor thought it home too soon.

Historically Leissègues landed a thousand men at Santo Domingo and was caught at anchor on 6 February 1806: five of the line lost, 1,510 killed or wounded, 1,156 taken. The Moniteur printed a doctored account.

Historically Haiti killed the French who stayed in 1804; Ferrand's decree of 6 January 1805 let his raiders sell the Haitians they took, and Dessalines marched on Santo Domingo, killing civilians at Moca and Santiago on his retreat.

Historically Ferrand could buy twenty days' bread in February 1805 and his credit from France had not come; the Emperor ordered flour bought in America and small expeditions of muskets and men (5 August 1805).

exhibit: ‘Slavery is forever abolished.’ — the Constitution of Haiti, 20 May 1805, Article 2: three years to the day after the law.
‘Nous avons osé être libres, osons l'être par nous-mêmes et pour nous-mêmes…’ — the Act of Independence, 1 January 1804, Boisrond-Tonnerre's draft.
deck.line: Sire, Ferrand wrote {wrote} that he had bread for twenty days and no credit from France. The sea is open; two frigates can carry flour and muskets by the spring tide.
deck.watch: Blockaded {n} of the last 12 mornings — Decrès may write of Santo Domingo.
deck.counsel: Berthier — Two frigates and flour, Sire: the garrison thanks you in the spring and writes again in the autumn.

squadron.title: The Squadron for Santo Domingo
squadron.line: Sire, Ferrand wrote {wrote} that he had bread for twenty days and no credit; Your Majesty called it shameful to abandon these brave men. Brest can put five of the line to sea in a month.
squadron.counsel: Berthier — Five sail are five sail, Sire; Boulogne counts them too.

accept.caption: Send five of the line
accept.echo: Decrès: the squadron slips out of Brest on the night tide.
accept.situation: Five of the line are at sea for Santo Domingo; Decrès expects them home by {date}.
accept.remember: In {month} you sent five of the line; Decrès writes again of Santo Domingo.

home.line: The squadron is home from Santo Domingo, all five sail; Ferrand has his men, his flour and his muskets.
home.press: SANTO DOMINGO — The Emperor's squadron is home; the garrison is relieved.

caught.line: The British found the squadron at anchor off Santo Domingo: five of the line are lost; the men and the stores were ashore. Decrès asks for an inquiry.
caught.press: SAN DOMINGO — Our squadron sustained the honour of the flag against a superior enemy.

closing: Historically the Spanish colonists rose in 1808, armed by Pétion and Christophe; Ferrand killed himself after Palo Hincado on 7 November 1808, and the garrison surrendered to the British in July 1809.
Historically France recognised Haiti only in 1825, for 150 million francs paid to the former colonists; Mackau's squadron carried the ordinance, and Boyer accepted it on 11 July 1825.

accept.caption: Send flour and muskets
accept.echo: Decrès: two frigates clear Brest with flour and muskets for Santo Domingo.
accept.situation: Two frigates are at sea for Santo Domingo with flour and muskets; the garrison is provisioned by the spring.
accept.press: SANTO DOMINGO — Two frigates have carried His Majesty's flour and muskets to General Ferrand.
accept.remember: In {month} you sent flour and muskets; Decrès writes again of Santo Domingo.

decline.caption: Ferrand must hold alone
decline.echo: Decrès files Ferrand's letter; the garrison of Santo Domingo holds alone.
decline.situation: Ferrand's letter is filed at the Marine; the garrison of Santo Domingo holds alone.
decline.press: SANTO DOMINGO — General Ferrand holds the city for His Majesty.
decline.remember: In {month} you left Ferrand to hold alone; Decrès writes again of Santo Domingo.

deck.title: The Magazines
deck.source: the frontier magazines of Strasbourg, Mainz and Ulm and the field magazines of the 1805 campaign (Bertaud, 'L'armée de terre à la veille de la campagne de 1805', napoleon.org; Bergerot, Daru, intendant général de la Grande Armée); Daru Intendant-General from 1805, of the Grande Armée from October 1806 (Britannica)
deck.record: Historically the Grande Armée marched from magazines stocked before it moved — Strasbourg, Mainz and the depots raised along the road — and lived on the country only when they ran dry.

variants.text: The magazines were stocked once before; Daru asks for the convoys again.

deck.line: Sire, the magazines of the Rhine hold bread for a fortnight. Give me the sum and the convoys, and the corps will march a week without a requisition.
deck.watch: The army in the field, or a storm gathering: {m} of 2 mornings — Daru may write of the magazines.
deck.counsel: Berthier — A full magazine is a corps that arrives, Sire; an empty one is a corps that forages.

edict.name: the Magazines
edict.court_press: {SEAT} — The court of {court} contracts for its magazines.

accept.caption: Stock the magazines
accept.echo: Daru: the contracts are signed; the convoys roll for the Rhine depots tonight.
accept.situation: The magazines are stocked; the fed provinces carry a quarter more men until {until}.
accept.press: PARIS — The Intendance contracts for the magazines of the Grande Armée.
accept.remember: In {month} you stocked the magazines; Daru writes again.

decline.caption: Let the army forage
decline.remember: In {month} the magazines waited; Daru writes again.

deck.title: The Remounts
deck.source: the remount service of the War Administration — the Prussian horses of 1806 entrusted to Bourcier and the remount depot at Potsdam (Petre, Napoleon's Campaign in Poland); Dejean Minister of War Administration March 1802 – January 1810, then Lacuée de Cessac (napoleon.org)

voice.speaker: named
voice.name: Lacuée de Cessac, Minister of War Administration

deck.record: Historically the cavalry was remounted between campaigns by purchase and requisition — the Prussian studs after Jena, the depots that refilled the squadrons before Friedland.

variants.text: The depots were filled once before; the War Administration asks for the fairs' credit again.

deck.line: Sire, the depots hold more saddles than horses. A credit now buys remounts in the country at the spring fairs' price, not the campaign's.
deck.watch: The horse at {n}% of its establishment, depots or squadrons — the War Administration may write of remounts.
deck.counsel: Berthier — A squadron without horses is infantry that eats oats, Sire.

edict.name: the Remounts
edict.court_press: {SEAT} — The court of {court} buys remounts for its horse.

accept.caption: Buy the remounts
accept.echo: The War Administration: the remount agents ride for the fairs; the depots fill by the month's end.
accept.situation: The remounts are bought; cavalry levies cost a fifth less until {until}.
accept.press: PARIS — The War Administration buys remounts for the cavalry of the Grand Army.
accept.remember: In {month} you bought the remounts; the War Administration writes again.

decline.caption: Let the depots wait
decline.remember: In {month} the depots waited; the War Administration writes again.

deck.title: The Camps of Instruction
deck.source: the camps of the Army of the Ocean Coasts, 1803–05 — Boulogne and Saint-Omer under Soult, Montreuil under Ney, Bruges under Davout — raised 17 August 1805 (Bertaud, napoleon.org; history-pas-de-calais.com); Berthier Minister of War to 9 August 1807, then Clarke
deck.record: Historically the camps of Boulogne drilled a conscript army through two years of peace into the Grande Armée that marched to Ulm; a peace with camps of instruction was the Empire's habit.

variants.text: The camps were formed once before; the Minister of War asks for the grounds again.

deck.line: Sire, the regiments idle in their garrisons. Four months of camps — the Boulogne drill, the divisions manoeuvring together — would give Your Majesty an army, not a muster.
deck.watch: At peace {m} of 6 mornings, the chest idle — the Minister of War may write of the camps.
deck.counsel: Talleyrand — A camp is a peace that looks like a war, Sire; Europe will read it so.

edict.name: the Camps of Instruction
edict.court_press: {SEAT} — The court of {court} forms camps of instruction for its army.

accept.caption: Form the camps
accept.echo: The Minister of War: the camps are ordered; the first divisions march to their grounds within the month.
accept.situation: The camps of instruction are formed; every drill yields five more morale until {until}.
accept.press: PARIS — The Minister of War forms camps of instruction for the regiments of the line.
accept.remember: In {month} you formed the camps; the Minister of War writes again.

decline.caption: Let the regiments rest
decline.remember: In {month} the camps waited; the Minister of War writes again.
